### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/mcp`, `@objectstack/runtime`, touching **8** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/mcp/README.md`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**2** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/permissions/authorization.mdx`  _(via buildMcpBridge (symbol, a top-level function))_
- `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`  _(via handleMcpRequest (symbol, a top-level function))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/mcp/README.md`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `sys_user (literal, 56 pages)`
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **37** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 493ad095d40ece94fe25d822566138fd01f5d4c3` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `20ebfb2cb3d4468609c9d02d28ef2c46a9f509ca` — the merge of head `183bed4d56f62825853b772d7076a4b5af29b8af` into base `493ad095d40ece94fe25d822566138fd01f5d4c3`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 20ebfb2cb3d4468609c9d02d28ef2c46a9f509ca && git checkout 20ebfb2cb3d4468609c9d02d28ef2c46a9f509ca
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 493ad095d40ece94fe25d822566138fd01f5d4c3 183bed4d56f62825853b772d7076a4b5af29b8af && git checkout -B drift-repro 493ad095d40ece94fe25d822566138fd01f5d4c3 && git merge --no-ff 183bed4d56f62825853b772d7076a4b5af29b8af

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 493ad095d40ece94fe25d822566138fd01f5d4c3
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 493ad095d40ece94fe25d822566138fd01f5d4c3` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

repo:objectstack#4 · os-elon-musk · session_016WV4d12FHULfLH9SigsWws

**L1 verdict (L1-a): ACCEPT** at head `3dae06ce43` (Fixes #35584: on a delegated OAuth token, the docs audience reads the delegating person's own permission sets, under maintainer ruling A 7043930931).

**Gates on this head:**
- `l1-face --pr 35888`: 37 success, 18 expected skip, 0 pending, 2 failed. Both failures are `Check Changeset` (`check-empty-changeset`), red by design on the declared DELIBERATE CORRECTION of `.changeset/35442-mcp-app-docs-tools.md`. Everything else in the face is ok.
- `Lint & Repo Gates` and `TypeScript Type Check` are both success. Dogfood battery not owed.
- Local at this head, after building the runtime's dependency closure: `vitest run src/domains/mcp-package-docs.test.ts` passed 1 file, 18 tests.

**Ruling A, condition by condition (holds):**
1. **Scope still decides reach.** `mcp.ts` builds the docs seam only when there is no grant or the grant includes `data:read`. That is the same condition as `packageDocToolsServed`, so a token without it never has the person's holdings read. Pin: `a token whose scope does not reach the docs tools…` (both members `undefined`).
2. **The delegator's own holdings, failing closed, never a union.**
   - `delegatingPersonOf` takes only `principalKind: 'agent'` with a non-empty `onBehalfOf.userId`.
   - `delegatorHoldingsCaller` throws on three cases: no `sys_user` row (read with `isSystem`), no membership in the request's organization (`vetOrganizationClaim`, the one membership rule, as `delegatedOrganizationRefusal` asks it), and no engine.
   - A throw reaches `resolveAudienceCaller` (`packages/rest/src/meta-item-read-gate.ts:700-707`), whose `catch` leaves `permissionSets` undefined, so permission-set audiences deny.
   - The returned caller is built only from the person's grants. It carries no `onBehalfOf` and none of the envelope's `permissions`, so there is no union.
   - With no `tenantId`, the resolver's no-tenant rule gives global grants only, as `resolveDelegatorContext` does (ADR-0123 D2: no active organization is not the membership rule's case).
   - The pins `the holder…`, `fails closed…` (ghost and out-of-org), `no union…` and `an AI service account keeps its own sets` are all in the diff and green.
3. **Non-holder control is kept, and a new OAuth control is added:** `control: a person who does not hold the set in the token's organization…` answers CLOSED.
4. **Not L1's:** security#2's read-only head check before merge.

**The DELIBERATE CORRECTION (35442 note), sentence by sentence:**
- Before: "On an OAuth grant that caller is the agent, so the docs audience is judged on the token's grant (its scope-derived permission sets), not on the person's own permission sets: a manual whose audience is a permission set the person holds stays hidden on that connection. Both tool descriptions say so."
- After: "On an OAuth grant the request is an agent acting for the person who consented, and a permission-set audience is read against that person's own permission sets (ADR-0090 D10), never the token's scope-derived sets."
- The new sentence is true of the code above, and it sits in a bullet that already says the tools register only for `data:read`.
- The dropped "Both tool descriptions say so." is fine. The new 35584 note states the new descriptions.
- Restoring the old sentence would put a false release note back, so the red is correct. This is a code-changing PR, so per landing-operations it also needs the seat's same-head at-tier contract PASS, which reads the rewritten sentence too.

**35584 changeset, sentence by sentence (holds):** scope decides reach (`data:read`); the person's own sets via grant resolution; nonexistent or non-member gets no set; no union with the token's sets; default audience unchanged; API keys, sessions and AI service accounts keep their own sets; both descriptions now say so. Both are true against the diff, and both packages (`@objectstack/mcp`, `@objectstack/runtime`) are public and listed as patch.

**`mcp-http-tools.ts` (text only):** two docblocks and two descriptions. The descriptions are shorter (−25 B and −29 B) and state the ruled audience ("the person's own permission sets decide, never more"). No test pins either string. The descriptions are an MCP-facing face, so the seat's Clause-② read covers them.

**Notes (non-blocking):**
- N1. The 35584 changeset says the person's sets are resolved "in the organization the token's consent bound". The code reads the request's `tenantId` (the PR body says "the request's organization"). On an OAuth envelope these should be the same organization. security#2 can confirm that in its head check.
- N2. The `data:read` condition is now spelled in two places (runtime and `packageDocToolsServed`). The PR's Acceptance notes say both must move together. A shared export would remove the second copy; it is not owed here.

**Landing:** seat contract read (Clause-② yes, widening; this is also the DELIBERATE CORRECTION's L2 confirmation), then security#2's read-only head check, then the seat lands with the by-design red.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `3dae06ce43bd442dce3f5b47aaffb26f160a320f`
Local-runs: none
Security-touching: yes

Face: the `Clause-②: yes` declaration alone. The six-file list holds no `packages/spec/src` path and no governed path, and neither the PR body nor a changeset declares the `(narrowing)` arm, so `reviewFace` answers the declaration face, whose tier name is `TIER_DEFAULT`, exact. No `Scope:` floor, no ④ and no tier evidence are owed on this face. The run was the seat's isolated read-only sub-agent. Its transcript passes `verify-review-tier.mjs`, so it was served at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`; the line above still names the face's tier, because the committed tree decides the name and the name is exact in both directions.

Read: the net diff against merge-base `8145424b53` (6 files, +259/-58), card #35584 with every comment, the ruling record 7043930931, both dev reports (7045459701, 7062409108), the seat's final-head comment 7062718755, the L1 verdict 7062795354, the cited code in this head's tree, and the head's check-runs: 37 success, 18 skipped, 2 failed, 0 pending. Both failures are `Check Changeset`, and in both the one failed step is the foreign-changeset refusal on `.changeset/35442-mcp-app-docs-tools.md`; the ADR-0087 step and the major-bump step of the same job are green. Nothing was built or run.

Result: the code implements ruling A as ruled, and this read found no path on which a permission-set manual is served to a principal the ruling excludes. `Security-touching: yes` is meant: the hunks decide whose permission sets open a manual on a delegated token. No must-fix. S1 and S2 below are open on this head, and each earns a delta review of its fix. Both are text in published files; neither is in the code. The read-only head check by security#2 (ruling condition 4) is still owed before merge and is not this record's.

### ① Derived judgments

**Ruling A against the code**

- **Condition 1, the token's scope still decides reach: holds.** `handleMcpRequest` resolves the docs seam only when the envelope carries no grant or the grant includes `data:read`. That is the condition `packageDocToolsServed` registers the two tools on, and `registerPackageDocTools` is the only reader of the two bridge members. A token without `data:read` gets a bridge with neither member, so the person's holdings are never read for it. Pin: `a token whose scope does not reach the docs tools is carried no docs member, whatever the person holds`.
- **Condition 2, the delegating person's own holdings: holds.** `delegatingPersonOf` answers a person only for `principalKind: 'agent'` with a non-empty `onBehalfOf.userId`. `delegatorHoldingsCaller` builds the caller the security service is asked about from `resolveUserAuthzGrants` alone, in the envelope's organization. It is the same call and the same caller shape as the draft door's `resolveHumanReader`, without that door's `manage_metadata` admission, as the ruling asks. That caller carries nothing of the envelope: not its `permissions`, not its `onBehalfOf`. `resolveCaller` still answers the envelope, and the doc and book arms read only whether it has a `userId`, so the default audience answers as before.
- **Fail closed: holds.** No `sys_user` row (read under the system context, as `readSysUserRow` reads it), no membership in the envelope's organization (`vetOrganizationClaim` on the person's own `accessible_org_ids`, the rule `delegatedOrganizationRefusal` asks), no data engine, a security service without the verb, and any read that throws all end in the catch of `resolveAudienceCaller` (`packages/rest/src/meta-item-read-gate.ts`). It leaves `permissionSets` undefined, and `audienceAllows` then denies every `{ permissionSet }` audience. An envelope with no organization resolves the person with none, as `resolveDelegatorContext` does (ADR-0123 D2): no grant stored in an organization applies.
- **Never a union: holds.** With a delegating person, the envelope's ceiling sets never reach `resolvePermissionSetNames`. Pin: `no union: a manual whose audience is a set only the token's ceiling carries stays closed`.
- **AI service accounts keep their own sets: holds.** With no `onBehalfOf` the gate is the unchanged one. Pin: `an AI service account keeps its own sets`.
- **Condition 3: holds.** The session control pair is kept, an OAuth non-holder control is added, and the scope pin exists.

**Widening paths looked for, none found**

- A missing person: closed, and pinned (`ghost`: grant and membership rows, no user row).
- A revoked or changed set: holdings are read once per gate, and a gate is built per tool call (`createPackageDocMembers` reads its sources per call; the bridge is per request). Nothing outlives the call. The read is the shared resolver's, on the same terms as the person's own request.
- The organization: on this door the envelope's organization is the one the token's consent bound, kept only while a current membership backs it (`resolve-execution-context.ts`, then the session arm of `resolveAuthzContext`). It is never another organization the person belongs to. S2 is about how the new note words this.
- A cached failure: a rejected holdings promise is kept for the life of the gate, which keeps it closed.
- Listing: the runtime's scope condition and the MCP runtime's agree at this head.

**The DELIBERATE CORRECTION of `.changeset/35442-mcp-app-docs-tools.md`: accurate, and declared as the rule asks**

- Before (merge base): "On an OAuth grant that caller is the agent, so the docs audience is judged on the token's grant (its scope-derived permission sets), not on the person's own permission sets: a manual whose audience is a permission set the person holds stays hidden on that connection. Both tool descriptions say so."
- After (this head): "On an OAuth grant the request is an agent acting for the person who consented, and a permission-set audience is read against that person's own permission sets (ADR-0090 D10), never the token's scope-derived sets."
- The before sentence is false at this head, so restoring it from the base would publish a false note. The after sentence is true of the code. Its first clause is the agent arm of `assembleExecutionContext`. Its second clause is `delegatorHoldingsCaller`. "Never the token's scope-derived sets" is the no-union pin. Dropping "Both tool descriptions say so." is right: the descriptions no longer say that, and the new note states what they say now. The rest of the bullet (the gate, the not-found answer, the `data:read` registration) is untouched and still true, and nothing else in that note speaks of OAuth.
- The declaration: the PR body names the note under **DELIBERATE CORRECTION** and quotes the corrected sentence. No `skip-changeset` label is on the PR. The seat's comment 7062718755 names the gate and the reason. `Check Changeset` is red on exactly that refusal and on nothing else. The diff changes code, so this record is the confirmation `landing-operations.md` asks for, and it confirms the correction.

**`packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.ts` (text only):** both docblocks and both descriptions state the ruled audience and agree with the runtime.

**S1 (should-fix): `packages/mcp/README.md` still states the rule this PR replaces.**
- Lines 181 to 184 at this head: "on an OAuth grant the caller is the agent, judged on the token's grant rather than the person's own permission sets". The file is not in the diff.
- It ships in the `@objectstack/mcp` tarball this PR bumps. It is the same stated limit of PR #35564 that the card's Done-when asks to remove or keep to match: the descriptions, the changeset and the helper header were corrected, and this copy was missed. After this head lands, the package's own README says a holder cannot read a manual that the runtime serves to them.
- To close it: the same one-sentence correction on this branch, under an amended claim, or the seat's carrier card before landing. A search of the head for the old sentence finds no other copy in `content/docs`, `skills` or the other READMEs.

**S2 (should-fix, changeset text): the new note's organization sentences say more than the door does.**
- `.changeset/35584-delegated-docs-audience.md`, second bullet: "…in the organization the token's consent bound. A person who does not exist, or who holds no current membership in that organization, holds no set here, and permission-set manuals stay closed to them."
- The code reads the envelope's organization (`caller.tenantId`). The PR body and the helper header say that correctly ("the organization the request runs in"). On this door it is the consent's organization only while a current membership backs it. Once none does, the identity step has already dropped it, and the person is read with no active organization, as their own session is (ADR-0123). The membership vet inside the gate is a second asking of the same rule.
- So "holds no set here" is exact for a person with no user row and for the gate's own vet. For a person whose membership has ended, the note should say what the door does. Suggested: "…in the organization the request runs in: the one the token's consent bound, while the person's membership there is current. A person with no user row holds no set here. A person whose membership there has ended is read with no active organization, as their own session is, so no grant stored in an organization applies."
- This is L1 note N1, answered: on a token-only request the two cannot name different organizations, and the mismatch is wording. A changeset is a prose face, so this correction keeps the record on the new head under a `Regen-provenance:` line.

Nits, none of which moves this head by itself:

- Nit a. Two of the fail-closed arms the helper header names have no pin at this seam: no data engine, and a user or grants read that throws. They rest on the gate's catch, which `packages/rest/src/meta-app-nav-doc-audience.test.ts` pins for the REST door. The membership pin drives a hand-built envelope, with an organization the identity step would have dropped. A second case through `oauthEnvelope`, for a person with a grant row and no membership in the consent's organization, would pin what the door itself answers.
- Nit b. A holdings failure is silent. The gate reads the throw as unresolved and nothing logs it, where `resolveHumanReader` beside it warns. On a host that resolves no data engine, every permission-set manual closes on every OAuth connection with no line saying why, which is the card's own symptom again. One `warn` for the no-engine and unreadable-grants arms (not for a missing person or a non-member) would make that absence loud.
- Nit c. "Nothing served today is refused" is exact against every published release: the two tools are unreleased, and the 35442 note is still pending. Against `main`, a manual whose audience names one of the token's scope sets goes from open to closed on an OAuth connection. That is the ruling's no-union condition, it is pinned, and it owes no `(narrowing)` arm because no published accept set narrows. For the same reason the new note's "used to judge" describes a state no release shipped, and whoever compiles the release notes may fold the two notes.

### ② Semver level

`'@objectstack/mcp': patch` and `'@objectstack/runtime': patch` are right. Both packages are public and both are moved by the diff (the descriptions and docblocks; the gate and the seam). `Metadata-protocol: none` is correct: nothing an author can write changes, no key, value, type or default, and the `audience` key means what ADR-0046 §6.7 says it means. That kind alone sets the level. `Clause-②: yes` is the conservative and correct reading: on a delegated token a permission-set manual is now served to a holder, and two published tool descriptions change. Both lines open a line in the PR body and in the new changeset. `readClause2Line` reads `yes` with no arm: the word after the dash is prose, not the `(widening)` arm, and means the same. No `Skills-docs:` line is owed for kind `none`. The corrected 35442 note keeps its own frontmatter and declaration lines untouched. No ADR-0087 disposition is owed.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev reports 7045459701 and 7062409108: `open_questions` is empty. `security_findings: none`, which this read agrees with for the diff. The out-of-scope finding of the first report (the `mcp-http-tools.ts` text) is closed at this head. Deviations accepted: the `searchPackageDocs` member docblock corrected in the same text commit, `@objectstack/mcp` added to the changeset, the default merge-commit message, the model-free trailer.
- L1 notes: N1 is S2 above. N2 (the `data:read` condition spelled in two places) is accepted with the PR's own acceptance note: if the docs family ever changes, both move.
- SQL push-down: the diff adds one `findOne` existence read and one call of the shared grant resolver. No id materialisation and no in-app join.
- `Check Changeset` is red by design, as above. Whether the PR may enter the queue with that red is the landing seat's three-condition check, not this record's.
- The author is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`: no login note is owed.
- Ruling condition 4, the read-only head check by security#2, is open.
